The system was operating at higher speeds Thursday, a day after Trump spoke with Musk, according to U.S. and Ukrainian officials. Some Ukrainian officials said service hadn't returned to full capacity.

The restrictions had limited Starlink connectivity to equipment traveling at speeds above roughly 100 miles (160.93 kilometers) an hour, disrupting Ukrainian offensive drones and missile interceptors used to defend against Russian attacks.
For investors, the dispute highlights the political and regulatory risks surrounding SpaceX's

expanding role as a critical Pentagon contractor. The controversy raises questions about how much control a private company should exercise over military communications, particularly when service disruptions can affect battlefield operations and U.S. foreign policy.
Trump expressed frustration with the restrictions and sought to reverse them after the Journal disclosed Musk's role in imposing the slowdown. The White House and SpaceX
have offered differing explanations about whether Musk acted independently or at the administration's direction.

The restrictions followed public criticism by Trump and Musk of Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy over attacks on Russian diesel refineries, which Trump has blamed for rising energy prices. Trump has denied ordering the Starlink slowdown or knowing who authorized it.

Military analysts said restoring higher-speed connectivity could improve Ukraine's ability to conduct longer-range drone strikes and deploy faster interceptors. Preliminary reports from Ukrainian military units indicated that network performance had improved.

Vice President JD Vance defended Musk's concerns about operating Starlink in a war zone without clear direction from Washington. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth and Secretary of State Marco Rubio, meanwhile, have emphasized SpaceX's
authority to enforce its service agreements.

The controversy has further strained relations between Washington and Kyiv as Russia continues its aerial attacks on Ukraine. Moscow launched another major barrage against Kyiv overnight, despite recently agreeing to participate in U.S.-brokered peace talks.
Sen. Richard Blumenthal, a Connecticut Democrat, announced an investigation Thursday into the Starlink restrictions and the Pentagon's reliance on SpaceX
The inquiry could intensify congressional scrutiny of SpaceX's
government contracts and the potential national security consequences of relying on privately controlled communications infrastructure.
